title: Slow-cooker chicken stew with dumplings
subtitle: Hearty British chicken stew with fluffy suet-free dumplings
excerpt: Tender chicken thighs in a thick root vegetable broth, topped with light butter dumplings that steam on top in the last hour. A complete one-pot meal.
sourceNotes: Chicken stew with dumplings is a traditional British winter dish. These butter dumplings use self-raising flour and cold butter rather than suet, producing a lighter result. Documented across many British cookery books from the 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew can be made a day ahead. Make fresh dumplings and cook them in the reheated stew just before serving.

content.text: This is a two-stage slow cooker recipe. The stew cooks for 5 to 6 hours on LOW. In the last hour, homemade dumplings go on top and cook with the lid on, steaming in the heat of the stew. The dumplings will puff up and absorb the broth from below. They should be light and soft, not heavy.
Cold butter grated into the flour is the key to a light dumpling. Handle the dough as little as possible once the milk goes in; overworking makes dumplings dense.
This dish needs nothing alongside; it is a complete meal.

Add {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thigh pieces to the slow cooker with {{carrot}} of carrot, {{celery}} of celery, {{onion}} diced onion, {{leek}} sliced leek, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Tuck in {{thyme}} of thyme sprigs and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Pour over {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. In the last 30 minutes, stir in the cornflour slurry. Set to HIGH. This will thicken the broth. Discard the thyme sprigs and bay leaves.

Add {{self-raising-flour}} of self-raising flour to a bowl. Grate in {{unsalted-butter}} of cold butter and rub it in until the mix looks like breadcrumbs. Add {{whole-milk}} of cold milk and stir briefly until just combined. Do not overwork. Shape into 8 small balls with floured hands.

Place the dumplings on top of the stew. Replace the lid and cook on HIGH for 45 to 60 minutes. The dumplings should be puffed and cooked through. Check by cutting one in half; it should be light and dry inside, not doughy.

rows.symptom: The dumplings are dense and doughy in the middle
rows.cause: The dough was overworked or the slow cooker was not on HIGH when the dumplings went in.
rows.fix: Cook for a further 15 minutes on HIGH with the lid on. Check again by cutting one through. Next time mix the dough as little as possible and ensure the stew is on HIGH before adding dumplings.

rows.symptom: The dumplings are too wet on the outside
rows.cause: They are sitting in liquid rather than sitting on top of the stew.
rows.fix: They need to rest on the surface of the stew with their tops above the liquid. Reduce the liquid level slightly before adding them, or use a pot liner to push them above the broth level.

rows.symptom: The stew is too thin after adding the cornflour
rows.cause: The cornflour may not have been mixed to a smooth slurry before adding.
rows.fix: Add a second batch of cornflour slurry and stir well. Give it 15 more minutes on HIGH before adding the dumplings.

rows.cause: After 6 hours on LOW, boneless thighs may shred rather than hold their shape.
rows.fix: Shred it all the way and serve it as a shredded chicken stew. It tastes the same; it just looks different. Check at 5 hours next time.

content.text: Chicken stew with dumplings is a British winter staple. It belongs to the same tradition as Lancashire hotpot and beef cobbler. The dumpling recipe here uses butter rather than traditional suet, which gives a lighter result and avoids the need to find suet in a shop. The principle is the same: steam a simple dough on top of a broth until it swells and absorbs the flavour from below.
